Specify individual group transitions

Source: R/group_transition.R
group_transition.Rd

Constructs a group-specific transition process specification for a simulation model. The convenience function set_group_tansition is equivalent to set_process(model, group_transition(...)) and allows for direct piping from a model.

Usage

group_transition(rates, group = NULL, weights = NULL, household = NULL)

set_group_transition(
  model,
  rates,
  group = NULL,
  weights = NULL,
  household = NULL
)

Arguments

rates

A nonempty data frame defining the mortality rate schedules. Must contain at least origin, destination, rate, and either age_start/age_end or dur_start/dur_end throughout. See details for format and description of stratification variables that can be applied.

group

The name of the declared group dimension (see set_groups()) whose categories are affected by this transition rate schedule. NULL (default) means the model's only dimension, and is an error when several are declared.

weights

NULL (default) for unweighted selection, or a weight_model() using person variables and destination, which chooses who in a cell moves without changing the cell's input rate.

household

NULL (default): each person moves individually. A household(): a move carries the mover's household with them on a transition. If the household is set, then the rates apply to the household collectively or individuals if they are not in households. Can only be used with age bands.

model

A hammel_model object, used by set_group_transition().

Value

group_transition() returns a process with a rates tibble; set_group_transition() returns the updated model.

Details

The primary and only required input to the function is a transition rate schedule for the rates argument. This data frame must contain either age_start and age_end columns or dur_start and dur_end columns to define the half-open age/duration intervals (inclusive at the start and exclusive at the end), an origin and destination column to define the origin and destination categories for the transition and a rate column for the transition rates. Transition rate are defined as the number of transitions from the origin to destination category per person-year spent in the origin category.

For a set of K categories, there will be K(K-1) possible transition rates at every age/duration band. Any cases left unspecified will be assumed to have a zero rate. The rates are not assumed to be symmetric (e.g.A > B is not the same as B < A), but users can provide schedules that make these rates

Each group dimension has its own transition process: and users must call set_group_transition() separately for each group dimension for which they desire a process. Columns named by declared group dimensions besides the focal group supply separate schedules for each combination of their categories; dimensions without a column share the same schedule.

Optional time_start/time_end columns select half-open calendar intervals in absolute years, including fractional years. Both columns are required together; starts are finite and ends exceed starts (possibly Inf). Active slices must satisfy the strata and coverage rules and cover the requested simulation run.

Transition rates can also be stratified by union_type containing either "partnered" and "unpartnered", or all three of "unpartnered", "cohab", "marriage", or by sex ("m" and "f").

Examples

# create grouped population
pop_start <- generate_uniform_population(
  1000,
  groups = list(ethnicity = c(A = 1, B = 1))
)

# create transition matrix with more A > B than B > A
ethnic_trans <- tibble::tribble(
 ~age_start, ~age_end, ~origin, ~destination, ~rate,
 0,          Inf,      "A",     "B",          0.05,
 0,          Inf,      "B",     "A",          0.02
)

# create simulation model and run it
model <- hammel_model() |>
  set_population(pop_start) |>
  set_fertility(usa_2000_fertility) |>
  set_mortality(usa_2000_mortality) |>
  set_union_formation("on_demand") |>
  set_groups(ethnicity = group(ancestry = TRUE)) |>
  set_group_transition(ethnic_trans)
pop_end <- run_simulation(model, 100)

# check population sizes - group A will grow relative to group B
calculate_population_size(pop_end, seq(0, 100, 20), by = "ethnicity")
#> # A tibble: 12 × 3
#>     time ethnicity population
#>    <dbl> <chr>          <int>
#>  1     0 B                497
#>  2    20 B                709
#>  3    40 B                767
#>  4    60 B                805
#>  5    80 B                825
#>  6   100 B                797
#>  7     0 A                503
#>  8    20 A                389
#>  9    40 A                351
#> 10    60 A                356
#> 11    80 A                331
#> 12   100 A                343
